'''Najat Aoun Saliba''' (Arabic: نجاة عون صليبا‎; Najat Khattar Aoun) is a Professor of Analytical Chemistry and an atmospheric chemist at the [[American University of Beirut]] (AUB). She was the Director of AUB's Nature Conservation Center from 2013 till 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Director|url=http://www.aub.edu.lb/natureconservation/Pages/ourdirector.aspx|access-date=11 November 2021|website=American University of Beirut|language=en-US|archive-date=11 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211111064246/https://www.aub.edu.lb/natureconservation/Pages/ourdirector.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref> Saliba is also the co-founder and director of Khaddit Beirut (an initiative launched after [[2020 Beirut explosion|Beirut's 2020 explosion]]) and the founder and director of the Environment Academy (an initiative created with the support of the [[World Health Organization]]).<ref>{{Cite web|date=10 May 2021|title=Najat Saliba|url=https://www.arab-reform.net/people/najat-saliba/|access-date=11 November 2021|website=Arab Reform Initiative|language=en-US}}</ref> She was appointed a laureate of the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards|L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science]] program in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=UNESCO |date=8 March 2019 |title=Najat Aoun Saliba: Push Forward Changes in Health Care Policies and Practices |url=https://en.unesco.org/news/najat-aoun-saliba-push-forward-changes-health-care-policies-and-practices |access-date=23 April 2022 |publisher=UNESCO |language=en | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190527200633/https://en.unesco.org/news/najat-aoun-saliba-push-forward-changes-health-care-policies-and-practices | archive-date=27 May 2019}}</ref> In 2022 she was elected to the Lebanese parliament.

== Early life and education ==
Born in 1966, Saliba grew up on a banana farm in [[Damour, Lebanon|Damour]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=The women of Lebanon: Najat Saliba, environmental conservationist|date=12 December 2020 |url=https://www.freiheit.org/lebanon-and-syria/women-lebanon-najat-saliba|access-date=11 November 2021}}</ref> where she was inspired by her father's connection to nature. When the [[Lebanese Civil War]] forced her family to move to the city, Saliba became interested in ways to mitigate air pollution. Saliba studied at the [[Lebanese University]], where she earned her bachelor's degree in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Najat Saliba|url=https://www.aub.edu.lb/tcrg/Pages/najatsaliba.aspx|access-date=27 May 2019|website=aub.edu.lb}}</ref> She moved to the United States for her graduate studies and earned her master's degree from [[California State University, Long Beach]]<ref name=":02">{{Cite web|title=IYC Profile: Lebanon {{!}} ACS News {{!}} Chemical & Engineering News|url=https://pubsapp.acs.org/cen/acsnews/89/8913acs1.html|access-date=27 May 2019|website=pubsapp.acs.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=LAU {{!}} SAS {{!}} Natural Sciences Department {{!}} News: Seminar on Pollution and Air Quality in Beirut|url=http://sas.lau.edu.lb/natural-sciences/news/all/seminar-pollution-airquality.php|access-date=27 May 2019|website=sas.lau.edu.lb|archive-date=27 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190527200625/http://sas.lau.edu.lb/natural-sciences/news/all/seminar-pollution-airquality.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> in 1994.<ref name="Najat Saliba">{{Cite web|title=Najat Saliba|url=https://www.aub.edu.lb/tcrg/Pages/najatsaliba.aspx|access-date=11 November 2021|website=aub.edu.lb}}</ref> She completed her doctoral studies at the [[University of Southern California]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Department of Chemistry|url=http://chem.usc.edu/graduate/ourgrads.html|access-date=27 May 2019|website=chem.usc.edu|archive-date=27 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190527200621/http://chem.usc.edu/graduate/ourgrads.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> in 1999.<ref name="Najat Saliba"/> She completed a thesis on [[water pollution]] and studied catalysis.<ref>{{Cite news|date=14 March 2019|title=Najat Aoun Saliba, les changements d'air du Liban|language=fr-FR|journal=La Croix|url=https://www.la-croix.com/Sciences-et-ethique/Sciences/Najat-Aoun-Saliba-changements-dair-Liban-2019-03-14-1201008650|access-date=27 May 2019|issn=0242-6056}}</ref> She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of California, Irvine]].<ref name=":02" />

== Research and career ==
Saliba returned to [[Lebanon]] after the Civil War, and joined the [[American University of Beirut]] in 2001.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://publiclab.org/profile/Najat|title=🎈 Public Lab: Najat|website=publiclab.org|access-date=27 May 2019}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> She helped to establish the Ibsar Nature Conservation Center for Sustainable Futures in 2002, which looked to protect Lebanon's biodiversity.<ref name=":02"/> She used to be the Director of Ibsar, which has since been renamed the Nature Conservation Center, at the [[American University of Beirut]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aub.edu.lb/natureconservation/Pages/what.aspx|title=What is AUB-NCC|website=aub.edu.lb|access-date=27 May 2019|archive-date=27 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190527200622/http://www.aub.edu.lb/natureconservation/Pages/what.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref> Saliba established the Atmospheric and Analytical Laboratory.<ref name=":1" /> In her early career she struggled to get chemicals, as the majority of Western companies would not ship to [[Lebanon]] for fear that they would be used to make weapons.<ref name=":02"/>

Her research considers ambient pollutants in [[Lebanon]] and the Middle East.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://en.unesco.org/news/najat-aoun-saliba-push-forward-changes-health-care-policies-and-practices|title=Najat Aoun Saliba: push forward changes in health care policies and practices|date=8 March 2019|publisher=UNESCO|language=en|access-date=27 May 2019}}</ref> Saliba investigates the toxic and [[carcinogen]]ic chemical constituents of [[electronic cigarette]]s and [[hookah]]s.<ref name=":2" /> She was the first to identify compounds such as [[formaldehyde]] in [[hookah]]s, and went on to show that [[electronic cigarette]]s can generate [[carbon monoxide]].<ref name=":2" /> She is part of the Center for the Study of Tobacco Products at [[Virginia Commonwealth University]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shihadeh|first1=Alan|last2=Saliba|first2=Najat A.|last3=Hage|first3=Rachel El|last4=Baalbaki|first4=Rima|last5=Karaoghlanian|first5=Nareg|last6=Khabour|first6=Omar F.|last7=Alzoubi|first7=Karem H.|last8=Soule|first8=Eric|last9=Salman|first9=Rola|date=1 March 2019|title=Toxicant inhalation among singleton waterpipe tobacco users in natural settings|journal=Tobacco Control|language=en|volume=28|issue=2|pages=181–188|doi=10.1136/tobaccocontrol-2017-054230|issn=0964-4563|pmid=29807946|pmc=6563915}}</ref> Saliba is part of a [[National Institutes of Health]] project to investigate the impact of smoking shisha.<ref name=":02"/> She was part of a $2.8&nbsp;million grant to develop computer models to analyse tobacco toxicity.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aub.edu.lb:443/articles/Pages/2.8-million-grant-tobacco-product-regulations.aspx|title=AUB receives $2.8 million grant to predict outcomes of tobacco product regulations|website=American University of Beirut|language=en-US|access-date=27 May 2019}}</ref> Saliba contributed to the [[World Health Organization]] Air Quality Expert Meetings.<ref name="aub.edu.lb">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aub.edu.lb:443/articles/Pages/Najat-Saliba-For-Women-in-Science.aspx|title=Najat Saliba laureate for Africa and Arab States "For Women in Science" award|website=American University of Beirut|language=en-US|access-date=27 May 2019}}</ref> In one of her works, she compared and analyzed air samples specifically related to forest fires from Beirut and Los Angeles where she draws conclusions about the differences and similarities that those countries share in terms of air pollution.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Plackett|first=Benjamin|date=28 April 2021|title=A Conversation with Najat Saliba|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/acscentsci.1c00424|journal=ACS Central Science|volume=7|issue=4|pages=510–511|doi=10.1021/acscentsci.1c00424|doi-access=free|issn=2374-7943|pmc=8155456|pmid=34056082}}</ref>

She established the first Lebanese atmospheric pollutants database. She became concerned about the open-air burning of Lebanese waste; and showed that the [[incineration]] could increase the amount of [[carcinogen]]s in the air by 2,300%.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dailystar.com.lb/News/Lebanon-News/2017/Mar-02/395719-experts-warn-against-waste-incineration.ashx|title=Experts warn against waste incineration |website=The Daily Star|location=Lebanon|access-date=27 May 2019|archive-date=27 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190527200622/http://www.dailystar.com.lb/News/Lebanon-News/2017/Mar-02/395719-experts-warn-against-waste-incineration.ashx|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://greenarea.me/en/104167/burning-of-waste-increase-carcinogens-in-the-air-by-at-least-2300-aub-study/|title=Burning of waste increase carcinogens in the air by at least 2,300% (AUB Study)|date=28 January 2016|website=GreenArea.me|language=en-US|access-date=27 May 2019|archive-date=27 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190527200621/http://greenarea.me/en/104167/burning-of-waste-increase-carcinogens-in-the-air-by-at-least-2300-aub-study/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She showed a variety of toxins are emitted during the burning of waste, and measured their concentration at the top of a four-story apartment building in [[Beirut]]. She identified [[Particulate pollution|particulate]] matter and [[polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon]]s as well as lead, cadmium, titanium and [[arsenic]] from metal burning. Saliba contributed to the [[American University of Beirut]] Guide to Municipal Solid Waste.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://issuu.com/ibsar-aub/docs/guide_to_municipal_solid_waste_mana|title=Guide to Municipal Solid Waste Management|via=Issuu|date=27 January 2016 |language=en|access-date=27 May 2019}}</ref> She established international protocols for the chemical studies of [[water pipe]]s.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://peerj.com/NASaliba/|title=PeerJ – Profile – Najat Saliba|website=peerj.com|language=en|access-date=27 May 2019}}</ref> Saliba develops innovative materials and methods to study atmospheric pollutants.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the961.com/people/meet-the-astonishing-lebanese-lady-who-just-made-international-headlines|title=Meet The Astonishing Lebanese Lady Who Just Made International Headlines|last=Srour|first=Maryam|website=the961.com|date=31 March 2019 |language=en-ca|access-date=27 May 2019}}</ref> In 2018 Saliba's [[American University of Beirut]] Nature Conservation Center was selected as one of the top influencing organisations in the regeneration movement by [[Lush (company)|Lush]].<ref name="aub.edu.lb"/>

Saliba also studied the effects of the [[2020 Beirut explosion|Beirut Port Explosion]] on the atmospheric pollutants in the city of Beirut.<ref>{{Cite journal |journal=Chemical & Engineering News |url=https://cen.acs.org/environment/pollution/Beirut-based-atmospheric-chemist-Najat/99/i22 |title= Beirut-based atmospheric chemist Najat Saliba discusses the challenges of doing science during political and economic turmoil |access-date=18 November 2021}}</ref> She also warned against potential hazardous chemicals and pollutants that were dispersed and called on the people of Beirut to take necessary precautions.<ref>{{Cite web|date=6 August 2020|title=Beirut blast may have left blanket of hazardous dust over city, says expert|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/world/mena/beirut-blast-may-have-left-blanket-of-hazardous-dust-over-city-says-expert-1.1060148|access-date=18 November 2021|website=The National}}</ref>

Saliba is an editor of ''[[PeerJ]]''.<ref name=":3" />

She was featured in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' in 2022 in the "Where I Work" session, describing her work connecting researchers and the local community.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Plackett |first=Benjamin |date=11 April 2022 |title=A grass-roots science movement to rebuild Lebanon |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=604 |issue=7905 |pages=394 |doi=10.1038/d41586-022-01000-x|pmid=35411066|bibcode=2022Natur.604..394P |s2cid=248099837 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== In politics ==
Najat Saliba became involved politically after the [[2020 Beirut explosion|2020 Beirut Port Explosion]]. She ran in the [[2022 Lebanese general election]] as a new face against the 50-year ruling political class. She won a seat in the parliament representing the Maronite sect of the [[Chouf district]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 May 2022 |title=The opposition forces make a breakthrough in Chouf-Aley |url=https://today.lorientlejour.com/article/1299778/the-opposition-forces-make-a-breakthrough-in-chouf-aley.html |access-date=4 June 2022 |website=L'Orient Today}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=News· |first=961 Staff·Lebanon |date=27 April 2022 |title=Here's The Detailed List Of Who's Running In The Lebanese Elections In 2022 |url=https://www.the961.com/list-of-candidates-by-district-lebanese-elections-2022/ |access-date=16 May 2022 |website=961 |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 18 March 2026, Saliba called on [[Hezbollah]] to hand over its weapons to the Lebanese government to strengthen the state, arguing that this move was supported by most Lebanese.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gCNeDWCI0vo |title=🔴 Al Jazeera English {{!}} Live |date=9 March 2023 |last=Al Jazeera English |access-date=18 March 2026 |via=YouTube}}</ref>
